chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) accepted the Jizyah from the People of the Covenant on the condition that they do not consume usury, do not eat the meat of pigs, and do not marry sisters, nor the daughters of brothers, nor the daughters of sisters. Whoever among them does that, the covenant of God and His Messenger is released from them, and they have no covenant today.

And it is possible that the report is specific to one who did not originally have a covenant, in that he is in the House of War. For if that is the case, the woman is awaited until her waiting period expires. If he converts before that, he has more right to her. And if her waiting period expires and he does not convert, then she has mastery over herself.
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions of the Jizyah covenant for People of the Book according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani’s chain in al-Istibsar clarifies that the Prophet’s acceptance of Jizyah was contingent upon specific behavioral prohibitions—such as avoiding usury and pork—which, if violated, nullify the covenant of protection (Dhimma). It further elucidates the legal nuance regarding mixed-faith couples in Dar al-Harb, establishing that a woman’s conversion prior to the expiration of her waiting period (Iddah) grants her husband priority, whereas her independence is secured if she remains non-Muslim. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the conditional nature of the Dhimma pact and its practical application in family law.
